title: Which shape do two crossing rubber bands make?
description: Two equal rubber bands cross at right angles at their middles, and joining the ends makes a square. Pulling one band out at both ends keeps the right angle and the middles, so the shape becomes a rhombus. Keeko doubts that it is still a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: diagonals that bisect each other at a right angle give equal sides, and equal diagonals decide between a square and a rhombus. Watch for students who name a square from the right angle alone.

source: Place two rubber bands perpendicular to each other, forming diagonals of equal length. Join the ends. What is the quadrilateral? Extend one of the diagonals on both sides by 2 cm. What quadrilateral will you get now?
video_script.why: The child sees that the diagonals decide the shape: equal diagonals that cross at right angles make a square, and unequal ones make a rhombus.
video_script.substitution: the book's own geoboard activity with two equal rubber bands and an extension of 2 cm at each end of one band
video_script.anchor: two equal rubber bands crossing at right angles on a geoboard, with their ends joined
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the shape is still a square because the bands still cross at right angles, but the diagonals are no longer equal.
video_script.payoff_line: The first shape is a square and the second is a rhombus

final_answer.value: First a square; after extending one diagonal, a rhombus
final_answer.spoken: first a square, and after extending one band a rhombus

hold_back: First a square; after extending one diagonal, a rhombus
never_show: the extended shape named a square
maths_rules: equal diagonals that bisect each other make a rectangle
diagonals that also meet at 90 degrees make four matching triangles at the crossing, so all four sides are equal, and a rectangle with equal sides is a square
extending one diagonal by 2 cm at each end keeps its midpoint at the crossing and the angle at 90 degrees, so all four sides are still equal
the diagonals are now different lengths, so it is not a rectangle and not a square; it is a rhombus
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonals decide the shape. One geoboard picture stays on the board and the longer band is drawn in after step three.
open_questions: The book places the bands perpendicular with equal length but does not say they cross at their middles; the worklist adds that, and the book gives no band length, so none is spoken.
